A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer-expressivity study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison; v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-recognition and language-modeling experiments in Tables 1 and 3, representation probing in Figure 2, and a masking comparison in Appendix F.2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1 and 3, Figure 2, and Appendix F.2.

M1.justification: The constructive simulator in Appendix B.3 replaces infinite attention parameters with a finite large constant, adds rounding-correction feedforward operations, and replaces negated mirror coordinates with complementary coordinates. These modify the theoretical construction; the evaluated architecture and training objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve recognition languages, three language-modeling languages, and bbΣ* masking task. The new benchmark citations in v2's introduction do not correspond to additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The LSTM remains the recognition baseline in Table 1. The strict-versus-nonstrict masking comparison in Appendix F.2 also retains the same participants; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain training lengths up to 40, testing lengths 41–500, five transformer layers, width 64, one million training steps, batch size 128, and 512 samples per test length. Evaluation criteria are unchanged. Removing the optimizer description does not establish a changed training protocol.

E4.justification: The DFA-state representation analysis, linear and nonlinear probing discussion, and strict-versus-nonstrict masking experiment are retained. Figure 2 contains the same plots, and Appendix F.2 tests the same question with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Both report five random seeds and three learning rates, with maximum accuracy and mean accuracy accompanied by standard deviations. The new checklist reiterates existing uncertainty reporting without introducing additional runs or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All reported empirical values in Tables 1 and 3 and Appendix F.2 match. For example, RDP-1 language-modeling maximum accuracy remains 98.3%, and masking maximum accuracies remain 100.0% versus 95.8%. The qualitative probing findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Central proofs are substantively revised: Lemma B.5 receives a general argument, the maximum-score reasoning from v1 Appendix F.1 is expanded into Proposition B.8 for stabilized softmax, and Appendix B.3 adds rounding derivations and replaces the layer-normalization proof. Sections 4–5 revise DFA and probability definitions. Theorem 4.1 also drops the earlier minimal-DFA assumption, broadening its statement.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now explicitly restrict the characterization and impossibility claims to the NoPE idealization, replacing broader language about practical or standard transformers. The central logical equivalence and empirical length-generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges that fixed-precision LM outputs may not normalize exactly and explains the treatment of zero-probability prefixes. Appendix B.3 adds rounding-induced failure explanations. The empirical interpretations and Appendix H limitations concerning positional encodings and perfect-accuracy evaluation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a link to the authors' code repository and states that supplementary code is provided; v1 only identifies the upstream code source. Conversely, Appendix E.1.1 removes the explicit Adam-with-default-hyperparameters description. Hardware, runtime, and remaining experimental details are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for MMLU, BIG-bench, SuperGLUE, and IEEE floating-point arithmetic, while removing the Adam reference. The main positioning against earlier transformer-expressivity research and Appendix G's organization remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title and introductory prose, standardizes P/F and PODFA terminology, organizes proof explanations into named stages, and numbers DFA definitions. Acknowledgments and a checklist are appended, while the main section sequence and much of the narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The same three numbered figures and three tables remain. Figure 1 and Table 2 receive terminology updates, Figure 2 moves from the top to the bottom of page 9, and appendix displays are relocated. Table 3 is restyled without changing its data.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies scope, adds code-access information, and improves the layer-normalization argument through complementary coordinates. However, Theorem 4.1 removes the minimal-DFA condition needed for its equivalence, and the new FFN weights in Eq. (55) sum the ReLU terms that Eq. (53) subtracts. Useful clarification and partial proof repairs therefore coexist with new formal defects in central arguments. With unchanged empirical evidence, a reliable net quality direction is unclear.
